runs.t: Laser Facials
1. Hero & Intro

Pigmentation that keeps coming back, skin that looks flat no matter how much you sleep, the first few lines near the eyes. Most people who ask about a laser facial treatment in Delhi have tried creams for at least one of these and want something that works a little deeper.

A laser facial does that without taking you out of your routine. The laser works on the layers under the surface, where pigment and collagen loss actually sit, while the top layer stays largely intact. That's why most people go back to work the same day. It's a popular pick for brides and grooms short on time, though plenty of patients book it simply because their skin needs a reset.
Available at Dadu Medical Centre Vasant Vihar (South Delhi) & Rajouri Garden (West Delhi), under Dr. Nivedita Dadu.
2. How a Laser Facial Works

The treatment uses fractional laser technology. Instead of treating the whole surface in one go, the laser sends controlled energy into the deeper layers through tiny, separate zones. The skin around each zone is left untouched, which helps it heal quickly.

Those small zones prompt the skin's own repair process. It starts making fresh collagen and elastin, the proteins that keep skin firm and springy. This is also why results aren't instant in the way a regular facial's are. The skin keeps improving over the weeks that follow each session.

The settings are adjusted for every patient, depending on skin type, how sensitive it is and what you want treated. So two people getting a laser facial on the same day may not get the same treatment.
3. Concerns a Laser Facial Can Help With

Pigmentation is the most common reason people come in, especially the kind caused by sun exposure. Uneven tone and general dullness are close behind. A laser facial can also soften mild acne marks, rough texture and enlarged pores, along with early signs of ageing like fine lines, age spots and the first bit of skin laxity.
If you have more than one of these, the settings can be adjusted to work on them in the same session.

Worth knowing: a laser facial improves skin quality. It won't change the shape of your face, and deep wrinkles or heavy sagging usually need a different treatment. Your dermatologist will tell you honestly if that's the case.

5. Ideal Candidates

Working professionals who can't take days off are a good fit, and so are brides and grooms with a wedding coming up and not much time left. More broadly, it suits men and women of different ages who are dealing with pigmentation, dull skin, mild acne marks or early ageing.
When it may need to wait:

A consultation comes first for a reason. Your dermatologist will check whether a laser facial is right for you now or whether it's better to delay, for example if you have an active skin infection or cold sore, a fresh tan, are pregnant, have recently taken oral acne medicine such as isotretinoin, or tend to form raised scars or keloids. Please share your full medical history and any medicines you take.

6. Process & Techniques
Skin assessment:
A dermatologist examines your skin and goes over your concerns, medical history and current skincare. This decides whether a laser facial suits you at all.
Setting the parameters:
Based on that assessment, the laser settings are chosen for your skin type, sensitivity and concern.
The treatment:
The laser is passed over the face in the clinic. Most people feel mild warmth or a slight tingling.
Follow-ups:
You come back for review so the doctor can track progress and decide whether more sessions or maintenance would help.
Sessions:
Most patients see a visible difference within two to four sessions, and the skin keeps improving in the weeks after. Your dermatologist will advise how far apart to space them.
(Session spacing and duration are not listed on the current page: to be confirmed by the clinic.)
Recovery and side effects:

There's usually no real downtime. Some mild redness or warmth right after the session is normal and tends to settle quickly. Results vary from person to person, and laser treatments do carry a small risk of side effects such as irritation or temporary changes in pigmentation, which is one more reason they should only be done by trained doctors with the right settings.
Aftercare:

Sunscreen isn't optional here. Skin is more sensitive to the sun while it heals, so apply it daily and reapply when you're outdoors. Keep up a simple skincare routine your doctor approves, and don't skip the follow-up visits. With good sun protection, results can last from several months to over a year.

9. FAQs
Q: What can a laser facial help with?
Ans. Dull skin, pigmentation, uneven tone, mild acne marks and early signs of ageing. It improves overall skin quality rather than changing your features.
Q: Will I need to take time off?
Ans. Usually not. Most people return to work the same day, with maybe some mild redness that settles soon.
Q: Does it hurt?
Ans. Most patients feel only mild warmth or a slight tingle during the session, and it fades quickly.
Q: How many sessions will I need?
Ans. Most people notice improvement within two to four sessions. Your dermatologist will suggest a plan after seeing your skin.
Q: Is a laser facial safe for Indian skin?
Ans. Yes, when it's done by experienced doctors who choose the right settings for your skin tone. That's why the consultation matters.
Q: Can it treat pigmentation and acne marks together?
Ans. Yes. The settings can be adjusted to work on more than one concern in a single session.
Q: Is it a good option before a wedding?
Ans. It's often chosen by brides and grooms because recovery is minimal. Starting a few weeks ahead gives the collagen time to build.
Q: How long do the results last?
Ans. From several months to over a year, depending on your skin, sun protection and skincare routine. Results vary from person to person.
